}
WORD_CAT = {w: c for c, ws in CATEGORY_WORDS.items() for w in ws}

# Conventional order, used only where the examples are silent (see note below).
ASSUMED = ["opinion", "size", "age", "shape", "material", "color", "purpose", "origin"]
IDX = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(ASSUMED)}

OPTIONS = {

    "C": "triangular old-fashioned iron pink eating turkish midsize canvas",

    "J": "medium-size plastic white walking bangladeshi old rectangular hat",

# 1. Parse the 75 example phrases.

# 2. Precedence edges (a must precede b) from every adjective pair in the examples.
edges = set()
for ph in phrases:

    adj = [WORD_CAT[t] for t in toks[:-1] if t in WORD_CAT]  # last token is the head noun
    for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(len(adj)), 2):

# 3. Transitive closure and consistency checks.

print("CHECK PASS" if acyclic else "CHECK FAIL")

def judge(words):

    det, ass, und = [], [], 0
    for (w1, c1), (w2, c2) in itertools.combinations(adj, 2):
        if c1 == c2 or reach[c1][c2]:

        if reach[c2][c1]:
            det.append(f"{w1} before {w2}")

            if IDX[c2] < IDX[c1]:
                ass.append(f"{w1} before {w2}")

        status = "WRONG (under assumed order)"
    elif und == 0:

    else:
